cards.note: Host-plane settings plugin: the only extension point it calls is ctx.inject(['settings']) -> settings.register; no APIProxy and no ctx.remote call site.
Target is alpha.2 (not alpha.1) and the plugin produces no third-party persisted SessionEvents; corridor net state read together with A2-01.
No host-source patch, no internal session-view import, no client half; the tree touches no harness internals.
No launcher wrapper, SDK/ACP integration or hardcoded profile path; the bundle layer is consumed by the official launcher via dsh.bundle.patch.
No headless wrapper or stdout/stderr parser; package scripts are tsc and node --test only.
No tool presentation mode, PTC preset, dispatch waterfall or tool-related types in the plugin.
No tool policy, permission/approval plugin or web_fetch configuration; the layer only inserts the plugin row.
No custom loopback HTTP/WS/RPC route, no browser page, no /api route; no web client half.
Optional model-provider capability; this plugin is not a model provider and carries no settings-page patch or shim.
Optional localization capability; no i18n resources, no client half and no custom i18n patch.
Optional subagent selection capability; the plugin runs no subagents and carries no selector workaround.
Informational deployment/privacy card; the fixture issues no model requests and ships no adapter config, so no plugin code change.
No PowerShell/Bash persistence or Windows directory-picker compatibility workaround in the tree.
No official-LLM session-log egress configuration and no session persistence/watermark code.
No browser acceptance script and no boot-manifest consumer; acceptance here is profile boot plus the host-side activation check.
Registers no structured-question answerer; userQuestions is never referenced.
No resolveSessionPreset use and no agent-presets roots configuration.
No host UI/stream-timing code; isTokenDelta is not imported.
The fixture layer is insert-only and never restates dsh-base rows; telemetry/inventory defaults stay deployment-owned.
No direct @earendil-works/pi-ai dependency or import; only cordis/schemastery/dsh-settings are consumed.
No dsh.client half, no dsh-client-runtime import and no client inject list to clean up.
No client bundle to register; the host-side row already uses the bare package name ('h5-runtime-drift-fixture') as its name.
No session-timeline or user-message reads; the plugin only registers a namespace schema.
No composer/DOM manipulation; the plugin has no browser-side code.
Does not render MarkdownText or import ui-primitives.
No ctx.connection usage and no history/transcript read.
No subagent seed/persisted descriptors and no SUBAGENT_DESCRIPTOR_VERSION assertions.
No workspace navigation or directory-picker calls.
Persists no third-party SessionEvents, so the restored ignorable retention semantics have no producer seam here.
No ctx.remote/unary Remote call and no RemoteResult error handling; settings are read through the host service.

devDependencies aligned to the alpha.2 cohort, incl. dsh-brand as the declaration owner for SettingsNamespace; the plugin-local pnpm install tree was removed (generated artifact, not part of the shipped files) so the host's cohort-install check resolves the declared cohort from the release-date registry; typecheck/build/test and a skipLibCheck:false diagnostic typecheck pass on that cohort.
No startup wrapper or CI-matrix Node workaround in the repository; verification ran on Node 24.21.0, outside the 24.0-24.11.1 failure window.
Does not consume pluginInventory/list or validate PluginInventorySnapshot.
No client Remote usage; $host.home/isLoopback has no call site.
The fixture mounts no tool/agent packages and adds no peers; its layer rides dsh-base, which already mounts session-projection.
Namespace literal passed straight to ctx.settings.register (compile-time SettingsNamespaceInput), test double uses 'as SettingsNamespace', and settingsNamespace() no longer appears in any import.
